name: TrueCommunity – Social Network, Groups, Private Messaging & Courses for WordPress
author: Joy Codes

sections.description:
TrueCommunity is a full-featured WordPress community plugin that turns your website into a private, self-hosted social network. Your members share updates on a live activity feed, react and reply, build profiles, join groups, send private messages and complete online courses, all on your own domain, with your own WordPress user accounts.

There is no third-party platform to rent, no per-member pricing and no separate login to manage. Your content, your members and your data stay in your WordPress database, under your control.

Whether you are building a membership community, a course community for your students, a customer or support community, a niche social network or an internal team space, TrueCommunity gives you the core building blocks in a single plugin instead of five different ones.

Why choose TrueCommunity?

Most community setups on WordPress mean combining a social plugin, a messaging plugin, a groups add-on and an LMS, then hoping they work well together. TrueCommunity is built as one connected system, so the feed, profiles, groups, messages, notifications and courses all share the same members and the same design.

  • Everything in one plugin. Activity feed, member profiles, groups, private messaging, courses and notifications.
  • Uses your existing WordPress users. Members log in with the accounts they already have. No duplicate user database.
  • Built on the WordPress REST API. A modern, app-like interface, with endpoints that other clients, including mobile apps, can connect to.
  • Modular by design. Switch features on or off so your community only shows what it needs.
  • Multisite compatible. Activate it on the sites where you want a community.
  • Own your community. Self-hosted on your domain, with your branding and your rules.

Activity feed: the heart of your community

The activity feed is where your community comes alive. Members post updates, share media, join conversations and react to each other, much like the social networks they already use every day. A good feed gives members a reason to come back, and TrueCommunity includes the tools that make that happen.

  • Rich text composer with mentions, emoji, links and media
  • Image, video and file attachments with a built-in lightbox
  • Polls with live results, so members can vote and see the outcome instantly
  • Reactions, likes and bookmarks to show appreciation and save posts for later
  • Threaded comments for real conversations, not one long pile of replies
  • Pinned posts so important announcements stay at the top
  • @mention notifications, so people know when they are being talked to

Member profiles and directory

Every member gets a profile page that represents them inside your community. Profiles help members recognise each other, build trust and start conversations, and a searchable directory makes it easy to find the right people as your community grows.

  • Searchable member directory
  • Profiles with cover image, avatar, bio and location
  • Clean profile URLs such as /community/u/username
  • Friend (connection) requests so members can build their own network
  • Member blocking, so people can protect themselves from unwanted contact

Community groups: public, private and locked

Groups let you split a large community into focused spaces: a group for each course cohort, product, topic, region or interest. Each group has its own feed and its own roles, so conversations stay relevant and easy to moderate.

  • Public groups that anyone can see and join
  • Private groups for members you approve
  • Locked groups for closed, invitation-style spaces
  • Join requests, invitations, and admin, moderator and member roles
  • A separate activity feed for every group
  • Moderation tools to keep discussions healthy

Online courses: a built-in learning management system

Teaching and community work best together. With TrueCommunity you can create courses right inside your community, so students learn, discuss and support each other in the same place instead of jumping between a course platform and a separate forum.

  • Courses built from lessons
  • Quizzes with automatic grading
  • Progress tracking so students see how far they have come
  • Enrollment management to control who can take each course
  • A course member list for instructors

This makes TrueCommunity a good fit for coaches, creators, schools and training providers who want course content and community in one WordPress plugin.

Private messaging

Not every conversation belongs on the feed. Private messaging lets members talk one-to-one or in small groups, share files and mention each other, which keeps relationships active and gives your community a more personal feel.

  • One-to-one conversations
  • Group conversations
  • File attachments
  • Mentions inside messages
  • Unread counts and near-real-time delivery

Notifications and email

Members stay engaged when they know what is happening. TrueCommunity includes an in-app notification system for mentions, replies, messages and more, and customizable email templates so your messages look like your brand, not like a generic system email.

  • In-app notifications
  • Customizable email templates with your own logo, sender name and footer text
  • Choose which events send email, event by event
  • Mail is sent after the page response, so it never slows the site down

Control your community, module by module

Not every community needs every feature. A course-focused community might want courses and notifications first, while a social club might start with the feed, groups and messages. TrueCommunity lets you enable or disable Stories, Groups, Courses, Messages and Notifications individually, so members see a clean experience that matches your goals.

  • Your own community name, slug and light/dark brand logos
  • Dark mode across the whole interface
  • Per-page limits, upload size and attachment count you control

Perfect for

  • Membership communities that want a private space for members
  • Online course creators and coaches who want students to connect and learn together
  • Schools, academies and training providers with cohorts, classes and lessons
  • Brands and customer communities that want to keep conversations on their own site
  • Support and help communities where customers answer each other
  • Clubs, nonprofits and professional networks
  • Internal company or team communities

Who is TrueCommunity for?

If you want the feel of a social network or a group community platform, but you want it on your own WordPress site and under your own brand, TrueCommunity is built for you. It is a practical choice if you are looking for a BuddyPress alternative with a modern interface, or an all-in-one community and course plugin that does not require a separate platform.

Built for the modern web

TrueCommunity runs as a single-page React application on top of the WordPress REST API and uses its own independent layout system, so community pages look consistent and do not rely on your theme’s page layout. Its token authentication endpoints let mobile and other clients sign in against the same site.

What is coming next

TrueCommunity is under active development. Planned work focuses on deeper course tools, membership features and a mobile experience. Your feedback in the support forum helps decide what comes first.

External services

TrueCommunity can embed content from third-party services. It does not call any external service on its own and sends nothing in the background. These connections happen in the visitor’s browser, and only when a member adds or opens such content.

  • YouTube: used to display YouTube videos that members share in posts. The video is embedded from youtube.com and its thumbnail is loaded from img.youtube.com. Data sent: the video ID and the visitor’s IP address. No account or API key is involved. Terms: https://www.youtube.com/t/terms, Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • Vimeo: used to display Vimeo videos that members share in posts. The video is embedded from player.vimeo.com and its thumbnail is requested from the public oEmbed endpoint (vimeo.com/api/oembed.json). Data sent: the video URL and the visitor’s IP address. No account or API key is involved. Terms: https://vimeo.com/terms, Privacy: https://vimeo.com/privacy
  • Google Maps: used to display a map of the location a member adds to their profile. The map is embedded from maps.google.com. Data sent: the location text and the visitor’s IP address. No API key is involved, and no location is sent unless the member enters one. Terms: https://maps.google.com/help/terms_maps/, Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. In your WordPress admin go to Plugins > Add New and search for “TrueCommunity”.
  2. Click Install Now, then Activate.
  3. Open TrueCommunity > Configuration and set your community name and slug.
  4. Open TrueCommunity > Modules and choose which modules to enable (Stories, Groups, Courses, Messages, Notifications).
  5. Visit your community at yoursite.com/<your-slug> and invite your first members.

You can also upload the plugin ZIP through Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin, or place the truecommunity folder in /wp-content/plugins/.
sections.faq:
What is TrueCommunity?

TrueCommunity is a free WordPress community plugin. It adds a social network, groups, private messaging and online courses to your own website, without needing an outside platform.

Is TrueCommunity a BuddyPress alternative?

It covers the same core needs (activity feed, member profiles, groups and private messages) in a single plugin with a modern interface built on the WordPress REST API, and it adds built-in courses.

Can I build a private community with TrueCommunity?

Yes. Groups can be public, private or locked, so you decide who can see and join each space.

Do my members need separate accounts?

No. TrueCommunity uses your existing WordPress users. Anyone who can log in to the site is a member.

Does it include courses, lessons and quizzes?

Yes. You can create courses with lessons and quizzes, grade automatically and track student progress.

Can I use TrueCommunity as a membership community?

You can build a members-only community with private and locked groups. Dedicated paid-membership features are planned.

Can I turn features off?

Yes. Stories, Groups, Courses, Messages and Notifications are each a separate module you can disable from TrueCommunity > Modules.

Does it work with WordPress multisite?

Yes. Activate it on each site that needs a community. Network activation is intentionally not supported, because each site keeps its own community content.

Does it work with my theme?

The community runs on its own set of URLs with its own layout, so it does not depend on your theme’s templates. Your theme still handles the rest of the site.

Can members send private messages?

Yes. Members can chat one-to-one or in groups and share attachments.

Is there a mobile app?

Not yet. The plugin provides token authentication endpoints and REST data that a mobile client can use.

Why is there a public login endpoint?

The community exposes three token endpoints under compro/v1/auth (login, refresh, logout) so a companion mobile client can sign in against the same site. They are the only write routes reachable without a session, exactly like wp-login.php, and they must be public for the same reason. login verifies credentials through wp_authenticate(), so every login filter and security plugin on the site still applies, and repeated failures from one address are locked out for fifteen minutes. The token is signed with a per-site secret generated with random_bytes() on first use, stored in an option and never included in any REST response. It carries a fingerprint of the password hash, so changing a password invalidates every token issued for that account. The bundled web app itself uses ordinary cookie authentication and never touches these routes.

Where do I get support?

Use the plugin’s support forum on WordPress.org.
